Four people, so one hundred and twenty each.
It is one hundred and twenty each, if we split it equally.

detail.m: Well… Tom did not come on Saturday, so he did not eat dinner with us. Is it fair that he pays the same?
o: I think he should pay less for the food, but the same for the house.
It is not very fair. Maybe he can pay ten dollars less.
I do not mind. It is easier if everyone pays the same.
br: That sounds reasonable. I will calculate it.
You are kind. Simple is good.

me.m: And I paid for the petrol on my card, so some of you owe me more. How shall we do it?
o: I owe you one hundred and twenty. I can transfer it today.
Could you send me your bank details, and I will pay you back tonight?
How about we pay you by the end of the week?
br: Great! That is the quickest way.
That is fine, but please do not forget.
I will send them right after this call.

next.m: We should plan the next trip soon. How do you want to handle the money next time?
o: Next time, let us each pay a small amount in advance, so nobody has to pay everything.
I suggest an app to track who paid for what. It is easier for everyone.
We could take turns to pay, and share the bill at the end.
br: An app is a great idea. I know a free one.
Good idea. It stops one person paying everything.

calls.end: Brilliant. Thanks for being so easy to deal with. Talk soon!

calls.title: A short job interview
calls.role: a hiring manager at a small company
phrases: I have two years of experience in…
I work well in a team.

hi.m: Good morning, and thanks for coming. Let us start. Can you tell me a little about yourself and your experience?
o: I have two years of experience in customer service. I enjoy helping people.
I recently finished university, and I did an internship at a travel company.
I worked in a shop for three years, and now I want a new challenge.
br: Good. An internship gives real experience.
That is useful experience for this role.

strength.m: What would you say is your biggest strength?
o: I am good at solving problems, and I stay calm under pressure.
My biggest strength is communication. I listen carefully before I answer.
I am very organised, so I finish my tasks on time.
br: That is very useful in this job.
Good communication is important for our team.

weak.m: And what is something you are still learning to do better?
o: I am still learning to say no when I am too busy. I am working on it.
Sometimes I spend too long on small details, but I now use a timer.
My English presentation skills are not perfect yet, so I take a course.
br: I like that you are taking action.
Good, you have a plan to improve.

team.m: Can you tell me about a time when you worked in a team and had a disagreement?
o: Once, a colleague and I disagreed about a plan. We talked it through and found a middle way.
In my last job, we had different ideas. I listened first, and then I explained mine.
I try to avoid conflict, but I once asked my manager to help us decide.
br: Asking for help at the right time shows maturity.
That is a mature way to deal with it.

ask.m: We are nearly done. Do you have any questions for me?
o: Yes. When could I start, if you choose me?
What would a typical day be like in this team?
Could you tell me about the salary and the working hours?
br: We would like someone to start next month, if possible.
You would work with four colleagues and help customers by phone and email.
The salary is on the job advert, and the hours are nine to five.

calls.end: Thank you for your time. We will contact you by the end of the week.

calls.title: A faulty product
calls.role: a customer service agent at an electronics shop
phrases: I’d appreciate it if you could…

hi.m: Thank you for calling TechPoint Customer Care. This is Ama. How can I help you today?
o: Hello. I bought a pair of headphones last week, and one side has stopped working.
I am calling about a faulty laptop charger that I bought ten days ago.
Hi, I received a coffee machine yesterday, and it leaks water everywhere.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Sound problems are annoying.
Oh, I am sorry. Let us look into it.
Oh no, that does not sound safe. Let me help.

detail.m: Could you tell me exactly what happened and whether you still have the receipt?
o: It worked fine for two days, then it suddenly stopped. I have the receipt and the box.
It stopped working after I charged it overnight. I have the receipt on my phone.
I am afraid I have lost the paper receipt, but I paid by card, so you can check.
br: No problem. I can find your payment in our system.

options.m: Under our policy, I can offer you a replacement, or a refund to your card. Which would you prefer?
o: I would prefer a full refund, please. I have lost confidence in this model.
A replacement is fine, as long as it arrives quickly. I need it for work.
What are my options if the replacement is also faulty?
br: Of course. The refund will take three to five working days.
We can send a new one by express delivery.
If it fails again, you will get a full refund with no questions asked.

return.m: We will need the faulty product back. How would you like to return it?
o: Could someone collect it from my home? I would rather not go to the post office.
I can drop it off at your shop tomorrow after work.
I would appreciate it if you could send a prepaid label by email.
br: Yes, a courier can collect it. Which day suits you?
That is fine. Just bring the receipt and the product.
I will send the label right now.

close.m: I am sorry again for the inconvenience. Is there anything else I can do?
o: Yes. Could you confirm everything in an email so I have a record?
No, that is fine. Thank you for solving this so quickly.
Just one thing: does the new product have a longer warranty?
br: It has the standard two-year warranty, and I can add one more year free.
Of course. You will receive it within the hour.

calls.end: Thank you for your patience. Have a good day!

calls.title: A proposal in a team meeting
calls.role: a team leader running a short meeting

hi.m: Thanks for joining. You said you have a proposal about how we handle customer emails. Go ahead.
o: I would like to propose a shared inbox, so everyone can see which emails are already answered.
I suggest we answer all emails within four hours. The main benefit is happier customers.
I propose a weekly meeting to share the most difficult cases and learn from them.
br: A shared system could save a lot of time.
Learning from each other is useful.

benefit.m: What is the main benefit, and how much would it cost?
o: The main benefit is that we avoid double answers. The tool costs around twenty dollars a month.
It would cost almost nothing, but it could cut our response time in half.
I do not have exact numbers yet, but I can prepare a short report by Friday.
br: Good. Please include a simple budget in the report.
That is a reasonable price for this team.
That would be a real improvement.

concern.m: One concern: the team is already very busy. Will this not take more of their time at the start?
o: I see your point, but the first week is the only difficult one. After that, we save time.
You are right. Maybe we could train the team for one hour on a quiet afternoon.
That is a fair concern. We could try it for one month and then decide.
br: A trial is a safe way to start. I like that.
One hour is acceptable. Let us find a time.
Hmm, I hope that is true. We will see.

compromise.m: The others are not sure yet. Could you suggest a compromise, so that everyone is comfortable?
o: Could we compromise by starting with only two people for one month, and then review the results?
We could start with the most common questions and add the rest later.
I would be happy to adjust. What would make the team feel comfortable?
br: A small start lowers the risk. Good thinking.
I appreciate the open attitude. I will ask the team.

steps.m: Good. Before we close, could you summarise what happens next?
o: Let us summarise the next steps: I will write a short plan by Friday, and we start the trial on Monday.
First, I send the budget. Second, you get feedback from the team. Third, we decide next week.

calls.end: Great meeting. Let us follow that plan.

calls.title: Telling a friend difficult news
calls.role: a close friend who does not know yet
phrases: I’m afraid I have some difficult news.
I wanted you to hear it from me.
explain why you are telling them
I know this isn’t easy to hear.
I hope you understand my reasons.

hi.m: Hey, you sounded serious in your message. Is everything okay?
o: Not really. I am afraid I have some difficult news, and I wanted you to hear it from me.
I have been putting this off, but I need to be honest with you about something.
It is a bit delicate. Could we find a quiet moment to talk properly?
br: Of course. I am free now. Take your time.
You are worrying me a little. Please go on.
Honesty is always best between friends. Go ahead.

news.m: Okay. I am listening. What is it?
o: I have accepted a job in another country, and I will be leaving in two months.
I have decided to move abroad. It has not been an easy decision for me.
I am afraid I cannot join the business we planned. Something changed in my family.
br: Oh. That is a big change for us. Can you tell me more?
Wow. That is huge. I did not expect it.

reaction.m: I am honestly a bit shocked. Why did you not tell me earlier?
o: I know this is hard to hear. I was waiting for the right moment, and I was afraid of upsetting you.
I am sorry for not telling you sooner. I only got the final answer yesterday.
You are right to be upset. I should have trusted you earlier.
br: Okay. I understand now. That is quick for you too.
Thank you for saying that. It means a lot.
I would rather hear difficult things early, but I understand.

reason.m: Can you help me understand why you made this decision?
o: It is a big chance for my career, and I have wanted something like this for years. I hope you understand my reasons.
It was the trade-off between staying close to the people I love and following a dream. It was not easy.
I felt stuck here. I need a fresh start, though I will miss you very much.
br: I can understand needing a change. Honestly, I have felt that too.
That is a difficult choice. I respect that you thought about it.
You deserve a chance like that, truly.

support.m: I need some time to process this. But I do not want to lose you as a friend.
o: Take all the time you need. Whatever you need, I am here, and we will keep in touch every week.
You will never lose me. Distance changes things, but it does not have to end a friendship.
I understand. Let us meet next week, when you feel calmer, and talk it through properly.
support.re: Thank you. That helps me a lot.

calls.end: Thank you for being honest. Let us not waste the time we have left.

calls.title: Joining a gym
calls.role: a friendly receptionist at a gym
phrases: say you want to become a member
How much is it a month?

hi.m: Hi, welcome to Fit Plus Gym. Are you interested in a membership?
o: Yes, I want to join the gym.
I would like to know the price.
I am just looking today, thanks.
br: Of course. I will tell you the prices in a moment.
Great! You are in the right place.

goal.m: What do you want to do here? Lose weight, get strong, or just stay healthy?
o: I want to lose some weight.
I want to get stronger and build muscle.
I just want to stay healthy and relax.
br: Good goal. Cardio and classes will help you.
Nice. We have a big weights room.
Then yoga and swimming are perfect for you.

days.m: How many days a week can you come?
o: I can come three days a week.
Maybe only on weekends, Saturday and Sunday.
I am not sure yet. Can I try it first?
br: Yes, you can! We have a free trial.

trial.m: The free trial is three days. Which day would you like to start?
o: I would like to start on Monday.
Can I start tomorrow after work?
Do I need to bring anything with me?
br: Just comfortable clothes and a water bottle. We have towels.
Perfect. I will write your name down.

price.m: After the trial, the membership is thirty dollars a month. Is that okay for you?
o: Yes, thirty dollars is okay for me.
That is a little expensive. Is there a student price?
Can I pay every month by card?
br: For students it is twenty-five dollars. You need a student card.
Yes, you can pay by card every month.

join.m: Wonderful. Can I have your name and your phone number, please?
o: My name is Anna Tran.
Sure. My phone number is zero nine one two.
Can I write it on the form myself?
br: Of course. Here is the form and a pen.

calls.end: See you soon at Fit Plus!

calls.title: Returning a gift
calls.role: a clerk at a shop’s customer service desk
phrases: I would like to return this.
bring something back to a shop
Can I change it for another size?
Do you have it in blue?
say it is the wrong size

hi.m: Good afternoon. How can I help you today?
o: I want to return this gift, please.
Hello. I would like to change this shirt.
This sweater is too small. Can I change it?
br: Okay, you want to return it.
Okay, you want a different one.

size.m: Okay. What size do you need, and what color do you like?
o: I need a medium, in blue.
Do you have a larger size in black?
Can I see the same one in green?
br: I think we have that color.

receipt.m: Do you have the receipt with you?
o: No, it was a gift. I do not have it.
Yes, here is the receipt.
I think it is in my bag. One moment.
br: That is fine. Without a receipt, I can offer you store credit.

credit.m: Store credit means you can choose anything in the shop, but you cannot get cash. Is that okay?
o: Yes, store credit is fine for me.
Can I use it for shoes too?
I prefer cash. Can you ask your manager?
br: I am sorry, without a receipt we cannot give cash.
Yes, you can use it for anything in the shop.

why.m: Can I ask why you are returning it? It helps us.
o: The color is not my style.
My friend gave me two of the same thing.
It does not fit me. It is too small.
br: Ah, that happens a lot with gifts.
Yes, size is the most common reason.

finish.m: All done. Is there anything else I can do for you?
o: No, that is all. Thank you.
Yes. Where can I find the shoes?
Can I have a bag for this, please?
br: They are on the second floor, next to the stairs.

calls.end: Have a lovely day!

calls.title: Booking a dentist appointment
calls.role: a receptionist at a dental clinic
phrases: I would like to make an appointment.
Do you have anything on Friday?
tell the clinic if you are new
ask what to take with you

hi.m: Good morning, Bright Smile Dental. How can I help?
o: I would like to make an appointment.
I have a toothache. Can I see the dentist today?
I need a check-up and a cleaning.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Let me see if we have a space.

pain.m: How bad is the pain? Is it a little, or very strong?
o: It is very strong. I cannot sleep.
Only a little, but it is getting worse.
It hurts when I drink something cold.
br: Okay. I will put you first on the list.
That can mean a sensitive tooth. The dentist will check it.

day.m: Which day is good for you? We have free times on Tuesday and Thursday.
o: Tuesday is good for me.
I can only come on Thursday afternoon.
Do you have anything on Friday?
br: Sorry, Friday is full. Tuesday or Thursday are free.

time.m: What time works best for you? We open at eight and close at five.
o: I prefer nine in the morning, please.
Three in the afternoon is better for me.
What is the earliest time you have?

name.m: Great. Can I have your name, and is this your first visit to us?
o: My name is Mai. It is my first visit.
I am Tom. I came here last year.
My name is Sara. Do I need to bring anything?
br: Welcome. Please come ten minutes early to fill in a form.
Welcome back. We have your file.
Please bring your ID and your insurance card, if you have one.

calls.end: See you then. Take care of that tooth!

calls.title: A problem with your bank card
calls.role: an agent on a bank’s card service line
phrases: the payment did not go through
I did not make that payment.
you do not recognise a charge
Could you block my card, please?
How long will the new card take?
I would rather collect it at the branch.

hi.m: Good morning, this is Carlos from the bank’s card service. How can I help you today?
o: Hello, my card was declined at the supermarket yesterday.
Hi, I think I lost my debit card on the bus.
I noticed a payment on my account that I did not make.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Let us block it right away.
Let us look at your account and find out what happened.

block.m: I have blocked the card, so nobody can use it. When did you last use it, and where?
o: I last used it yesterday evening at a pharmacy near my office.
I used it this morning to buy a bus ticket, I think.
I am not sure, but I paid for lunch with it at noon.
br: No problem. I can see your recent transactions on my screen.
Thanks, that helps me check the activity.

check.m: I can see a payment of eighty-nine euros at an online store. Do you recognise it?
o: No, I have never bought anything from that shop.
Yes, actually, that is my order from last week.
I am not sure. Can you tell me the date?
br: Then I will report it as fraud and block the card.
Good, then everything is fine. Let me check one more thing.
It was on Tuesday at nine fourteen in the evening.

verify.m: For security, I need to confirm your identity. Could you give me your full name and your date of birth?
o: Of course. My name is Daniel Brown, and I was born in nineteen ninety.
Sure. It is Anna Lee, and my birthday is the third of May.
Can I confirm it with my customer number instead?
br: Yes, that works too. Please read the number on your letter.

newcard.m: I can send a new card to your home in three to five working days, or you can collect one at a branch tomorrow. Which do you prefer?
o: I would rather collect it at the branch tomorrow.
Please send it to my home address.
Can I use my phone to pay until the card arrives?
br: Fine. Please bring your ID with you.
I will send it to the address we have on file.
Yes, once the card is replaced you can add it to your phone wallet. We will send you a link.

wrap.m: Is there anything else I can do for you today?
o: No, that is all. Thank you for your help.
Yes, could you also raise my daily limit?
Actually, can you text me when the new card is sent?
br: I can do that. It will be active within one hour.
Of course. I will set up a text alert.

calls.end: Thank you for calling. Take care.

calls.title: Renting a car
calls.role: an agent at a car rental desk
phrases: I would like to rent a car for the weekend.
Do you have an automatic one?
ask for a car without gears
Do I have to return it with a full tank?
What happens if there is a scratch?

hi.m: Welcome to Sunway Car Rental. How can I help you?
o: Hi, I would like to rent a car for the weekend.
Hello, I booked a car online under the name Kim.
I need a small car for a week, for two people.
br: Let me find your booking. Yes, here it is. A compact car.
Of course. Let us find the right car for you.

type.m: What kind of car do you need? We have small city cars, family cars and vans.
o: A small city car is enough, I will drive alone.
A family car, please. We are four people with luggage.
Do you have an automatic one? I cannot drive a manual.
br: Yes, all our small cars are automatic. The family cars come in both types.
Then I recommend the family estate. It has a big boot.
A small car is cheaper and easy to park.

extras.m: Would you like any extras, such as a child seat, a GPS, or a second driver?
o: I would like a second driver, because the trip is long.
No extras, thanks. I will use my phone for the map.
Yes, a child seat for my four-year-old daughter, please.
br: Okay, a child seat. That is five euros a day.
A second driver costs seven euros a day. I will need their licence too.
No problem. We will keep it simple.

insurance.m: Basic insurance is included, but there is an excess of eight hundred euros. Would you like to reduce it to zero for twelve euros a day?
o: Yes, I prefer to be safe. Please add the full cover.
No, thanks. My credit card already covers rental cars.
That sounds expensive. What happens if there is a scratch?
br: If you get a small scratch, you pay up to the excess. With full cover, you pay nothing.
Good choice. I will add it now.
Fine, but please check your card terms. I will keep the basic cover.

fuel.m: Please return the car with a full tank, or we will charge a refuelling fee. Where will you return it, and when?
o: I will return it here on Sunday evening at about six.
I would like to drop it at the airport on Monday morning.
Can I return it after hours if the office is closed?
br: Returning it at the airport is possible. There is an extra fee of twenty euros.
Yes, there is a key box next to the door. Just take a photo of the fuel gauge.
Perfect. We close at seven on Sundays.

finish.m: Your total is two hundred and ten euros. Do you have your driving licence and a credit card for the deposit?
o: Yes, here are my licence and my credit card.
My licence is a Vietnamese one. Is that accepted?
I only have a debit card. Is that a problem?
br: It is fine if you also have an international permit or a certified translation.
We need a credit card for the deposit. A debit card is not enough, sorry.
Thank you. That is all I need.

calls.end: Enjoy your trip, and drive safely!

calls.title: Fixing a slow internet connection
calls.role: an agent on an internet provider’s support line
phrases: the connection stops again and again
The light on the router is red.
Could you email me a summary?

hi.m: Thank you for calling Netline support. My name is Carlos. What seems to be the problem?
o: My internet has been very slow since this morning.
I cannot connect to the Wi-Fi at all. The light on the router is red.
My connection keeps dropping every few minutes.
br: A red light usually means the router has lost the signal.
Okay, let us find out where the problem is.

restart.m: Could you switch the router off, wait thirty seconds, and switch it on again? Then tell me what you see.
o: Okay, I turned it off and on. The light is green now.
I did that, but the light is still red.
Can I do that later? I am in a meeting right now.
br: Good, that means the router restarted properly.
Then there may be a problem with the cable or with the line.
Of course. I will create a ticket for you first.

test.m: Let us run a quick speed test. Open any speed test website and tell me the download number you get.
o: It says about three megabits, which is very low.
I get forty megabits, so the speed looks normal.
The test does not start. The page does not load.
br: That is much lower than your plan. Something is wrong.
That is a healthy speed. So the line is fine.
Then your connection is very weak. Let us restart the router.

cable.m: Please check the cable between the router and the wall. Is it firmly connected, and does it look damaged?
o: It is connected firmly, but the cable looks old and bent.
I found it loose. Now it is plugged in properly.
Everything looks fine to me. I do not see any damage.
br: That was probably the cause. Please check the light now.
Then we should replace it. I will send you a new one for free.
Then I will schedule a technician to check the line.

wifi.m: Then the problem may be your Wi-Fi signal. Where is the router in your home, and where do you use your laptop?
o: The router is in the living room, and I work in the bedroom.
It is on the floor behind the sofa, close to the TV.
I use my laptop everywhere, even on the balcony.
br: Walls and distance weaken the signal. A Wi-Fi extender could help.
Routers work best high up and in the open. Try moving it onto a shelf.

wrap.m: I have noted everything in your file. Is there anything else you would like to check before we finish?
o: No, that is everything. Thank you for your patience.
Yes, could you email me a summary of what we did?
Can you call me back tomorrow to see if it works?
br: Of course. You will get an email within ten minutes.
I will arrange a call back tomorrow afternoon.

calls.end: Thank you for calling Netline. Have a good day.

calls.title: Reporting lost luggage
calls.role: an agent at the airport baggage desk
phrases: It is a large black suitcase.
Please deliver it to my hotel.
Do I need to keep the receipts?
How long will the search take?

hi.m: Good evening, baggage services. How can I help you?
o: Hello, my suitcase did not arrive on the carousel.
Hi, I think my bag was left in Frankfurt.
My suitcase arrived, but it is badly damaged.
br: I am sorry about that. We will need to document the damage.
I am very sorry. Let us file a report and find it.

describe.m: Could you describe the suitcase for me? The size, the color, and anything that makes it easy to recognise.
o: It is a large black hard-shell suitcase with a red ribbon on the handle.
It is a medium blue soft bag with a broken zip on one side.
It is silver and has a yellow luggage tag with my name on it.
br: Good, a feature like that really helps the search.
Okay, I have the size and the type.

damage.m: Please show me the damage and tell me what was inside. Was anything missing or broken?
o: The wheel is broken, and my laptop screen is cracked.
The handle is torn off, but I think nothing is missing.
There is a big hole in the side, and my camera is gone.
br: Valuable items are covered by a different form. I will give it to you.
I will note the damage and take photos.

contact.m: Where should we deliver the suitcase once we find it? And what is the best phone number to reach you?
o: Please deliver it to my hotel, the Park Inn near the station.
Send it to my home address, which is in Ho Chi Minh City.
I am staying with a friend. Can I give you her address instead?
br: A hotel delivery, then. I will need the hotel name and your room number.
We can deliver it to your home address, but it may take two more days.
Of course. Please spell the street name slowly so I can write it down.

essentials.m: While you wait, you can buy essentials, like a toothbrush and some clothes. Keep the receipts, because the airline may repay part of the cost. Any questions about that?
o: How much can I spend, and when will I get the money back?
Do I need to keep every single receipt for the claim?
No, that is clear. I will keep all the receipts.
br: Usually up to one hundred euros a day, paid within three weeks.
Yes, please keep them and send photos with your claim form.

wrap.m: Here is your reference number. You can follow the search online. Is there anything else I can do?
o: No, thank you. You have been very helpful.
Yes, how long will the search normally take?
Is there a number I can call if I do not hear from you?
br: Most bags are found within forty-eight hours.
Yes, the hotline is on the form. It is open twenty-four hours.
You are very welcome. I hope you get it back soon.

calls.end: Thank you for your patience. Have a safe journey home.

calls.title: Talking to a noisy neighbour
calls.role: a neighbour who lives in the flat above
phrases: I do not want to cause trouble, but…
Could we find a solution together?
As long as you let me know in advance.

hi.m: Hello? Oh, hi. You live in the flat below, right? Is something wrong?
o: Hi, sorry to bother you, but I wanted to talk about the noise coming from your flat at night.
Good evening. I do not want to cause trouble, but the music last night was really loud.
This has happened every night this week, and I really need it to stop.
br: Hold on, there is no need to be so harsh. I did not know it was a problem.
Oh, of course. Thanks for coming to talk to me directly.

defensive.m: I only play music a little after dinner. Honestly, I think the walls here are just very thin.
o: I understand that, and I am not blaming you. Still, the noise goes on until after midnight, and I have to get up at six.
You may be right about the walls, but the bass shakes my bed. Could we find a way to solve this together?
Fair enough. Perhaps I was too direct. Can we start again and look for a practical solution?
br: Thanks, I appreciate that. Let us start again.
Okay, I am willing to talk about it.
I did not realise it was that late. That is not fair on you.

reason.m: I work from home in the evenings and I usually play music to relax. What time does it bother you most?
o: It is mainly after ten, when I am trying to fall asleep.
The worst part is the bass, which I feel through the floor.
Mostly at weekends, when people are over until late.
br: After ten is a fair limit. I can respect that.
Ah, I can put a rug or a speaker mat under it.
Weekends are when my friends come. I will tell them to keep it down.

solution.m: So what would you like me to do? I am happy to meet you halfway.
o: It would help a lot if you could turn the music down after ten o’clock on weeknights.
Could you use headphones in the late evenings, and let me know in advance if you have a party?
I would suggest that we exchange phone numbers, so I can text you instead of knocking on your door.
br: Headphones are easy. And I can warn you before a party, no problem.
Good idea. A text is better than a knock at eleven at night.
Ten on weeknights is fine for me.

compromise.m: What about weekends? My friends come over then, so ten might be tough. Can we agree on something else?
o: How about midnight on Fridays and Saturdays, as long as it is not too loud?
I could accept that on one condition: you let me know in advance, and keep the bass low.
I am afraid midnight is too late for me, but eleven thirty would be a fair compromise.
br: Midnight at weekends sounds fair. Deal.
Agreed. I will text you ahead and keep the bass down.
Eleven thirty is fine. I can work with that.

wrap.m: Great. Thanks for being so reasonable about it. Is there anything else we should sort out?
o: No, I think we have covered everything. Thank you for being so understanding.
Just one more thing: could you tell your friends to keep the noise down in the stairwell?
Yes, let us check in after a week to see whether the new arrangement is working.
br: Sure, I will tell them. They tend to get loud on the way out.
Good idea. We can have a quick coffee and talk.
Same here. Have a good evening.

calls.end: Thanks again for coming up. It means a lot.

calls.title: Meeting your child’s teacher
calls.role: a secondary-school teacher at a parent-teacher meeting
phrases: I would like to hear your honest opinion.
Would it be possible for him to…?
What could we do at home?
Could you let me know if anything changes?

hi.m: Thank you for coming in. I wanted to talk about how Minh is doing this term. How do you think he is getting on at school?
o: Overall he seems happy, but he has been struggling with maths homework lately.
To be honest, I am a little worried. He comes home tired and often says he cannot concentrate.
I think he is doing well, but I would like to hear your honest opinion first.
br: I appreciate you being open. That is useful to know.
That is encouraging. Let me tell you what I have observed.

concern.m: In class, he is bright but sometimes loses focus in the afternoon. He also hesitates to ask for help. Have you noticed anything similar at home?
o: Yes, he often stays up late on his phone, and that probably affects his concentration.
Not really. At home he is talkative, so I am surprised he is shy in class.
He mentions that some classmates laugh when he makes mistakes, which might explain why he does not ask for help.
br: Sleep makes a big difference. A fixed bedtime routine could help.
Quiet children often open up once they feel safe. Let us work on that.
Thank you for telling me. I will keep a closer eye on that in class.

strengths.m: He is creative and writes very thoughtful essays. His weak point is maths, mainly fractions. What kind of support does he get at home?
o: I help him when I can, but my own maths is a bit rusty, so he mostly works alone.
His older sister helps him, though she is busy with her own exams.
We have been considering a private tutor, but I am not sure it is the best solution.
br: A tutor can help, but sometimes a small after-school group works just as well.
That is lovely. Peer support works, but she should not carry it alone.
That is quite common. Many parents feel the same about maths.

plan.m: Here is what I suggest. We can offer him a weekly catch-up session after school, and I will send you a short progress note every two weeks. How does that sound?
o: That sounds very reasonable, but how long would each session last, and is there any cost?
I like the idea of progress notes, although I would prefer to receive them by email.
I am happy with that. Would it be possible for him to join a group with students at a similar level?
br: Each session is forty minutes, and it is free for all students.
Of course, email is fine. I will use the address on file.
Yes, the group has five students at about the same level.

home.m: And what could we do at home to reinforce this? Small habits help more than long study sessions.
o: We could set a fixed homework time and keep his phone out of the bedroom after nine.
I could ask him to explain what he learned each day, which would show me where he is stuck.
Perhaps we should reward effort rather than results, so that he feels less pressure about mistakes.
br: Yes, routine matters. That alone could help his focus.
Teaching it back is one of the best ways to learn.
Praising effort builds confidence. Excellent idea.

wrap.m: Shall we meet again in a month to see how things are going? Do you have any last questions for me?
o: A month sounds good. Could you let me know if there is any change in his behaviour before then?
Thank you, you have been really helpful. I feel much more confident about supporting him now.
Yes, one last thing: is there any chance he could join the school’s maths club next term?
br: The club starts in January. I will put his name on the list.
Absolutely. I will email you the same day if I notice anything.
It was a pleasure. Minh is a lovely boy.

calls.end: Thank you again for coming. Together we can help him.

calls.title: Negotiating a deadline
calls.role: your manager, who set a tight deadline
phrases: I wanted to give you an early warning.
tell your boss about a delay in advance
What if I send a first version on Friday?
Provided that I can take Monday afternoon off…
I should have raised it sooner.
I will flag any risk in the weekly meeting.

hi.m: Hi, you wanted a quick word about the Hanoi report? I thought it was due on Friday.
o: Yes, that is right. Unfortunately, I am concerned that I will not be able to deliver it by Friday.
Thanks for making time. I would like to discuss the deadline, as the data is taking longer than expected.
Hi. I wanted to give you an early warning that the report might be late, and to suggest a solution.
br: Okay, thanks for telling me early. What is the cause?
I appreciate the heads-up. Let us hear it.

cause.m: What exactly is holding things up?
o: The client sent the sales figures two days late, so I could not start the analysis on time.
I underestimated how long the data cleaning would take, and I have two other urgent tasks.
Part of the data was missing, and I have been waiting for the finance team to send it.
br: So it is partly outside your control. Understood.
Thanks for being straight about it. That takes honesty.

options.m: I have to be honest, the board meets on Monday morning. What are you proposing?
o: Could I have until Tuesday noon, so that I can double-check the numbers properly?
What if I send you a first version on Friday with the main findings, and the full report on Tuesday?
I could finish by Friday if someone from my team helped me with the charts.
br: A preliminary version could work. Tell me more.
Resources are tight, but let us look at that.
Tuesday is too late for the board. I cannot do that.

push.m: The board will want the full numbers, not a draft. Can you give me a stronger reason, or another option?
o: I understand. In that case, I could work this weekend, provided that I can take Monday afternoon off.
The risk is that rushed numbers could be wrong, and that would look worse in front of the board.
Then what about delivering the summary slides on Friday and leaving the detailed appendix for Tuesday?
br: That is generous. Let us make it official, and I will give you the time back.
Fair point. A wrong number would be worse than a late one.
That could work. The board mostly reads the summary anyway.

agree.m: All right, let us agree on something concrete. What exactly will I receive, and by when?
o: You will receive the summary and the key charts by Friday at five, and the full report by Tuesday at noon.
I will send the main findings on Friday afternoon, and I will message you immediately if anything changes.
By Friday midday you will have the draft, and I will present it myself at the Monday meeting if you wish.
br: That would be great. It shows ownership, and the board will appreciate it.
Good, keep me posted. No surprises, please.
That is clear. I will put it in the calendar.

wrap.m: Good. And please talk to me earlier next time. How do you plan to avoid this kind of delay in future?
o: I will ask clients for their data earlier, and build a buffer of two days into every schedule.
From now on, I will flag any risk in the weekly meeting instead of waiting until the last moment.
Honestly, I should have escalated it sooner. I will set interim checkpoints for every large report.
br: A buffer is wise. I will suggest it to the whole team.
Yes, the weekly meeting is the right place for that.
I appreciate the self-awareness. Thank you.

calls.end: Thanks. Let us make sure this report goes well.

calls.title: Ordering catering for an event
calls.role: a sales manager at a catering company
phrases: I would like to order lunch for forty people.
Two guests have a serious nut allergy.
Is there any flexibility on the price?

hi.m: Good morning, Green Table Catering. How can I help you?
o: Good morning. I would like to order lunch for about forty people for a company event next month.
Hello, I am organising a conference for sixty guests and I am looking for a caterer who can handle dietary needs.
Hi there. We are planning a small team celebration, around twenty-five people, and I would like some advice on the menu.
br: For a larger event, we usually advise a buffet to keep the queues short.
For a smaller group, a seated meal or a platter menu works nicely.

style.m: Would you prefer a buffet, a seated meal, or finger food? And is it lunch or dinner?
o: A buffet lunch would be best, because people will be arriving at different times.
I think finger food is more suitable, since the guests will be networking and standing.
We would prefer a seated meal, because there will be speeches during the event.
br: A buffet is flexible. We will set up two serving lines.
Finger food works well. We recommend eight to ten pieces per person.
A seated meal feels more formal. We will need a clear timetable.

diet.m: Do any of your guests have dietary requirements, such as vegetarian, halal or allergies?
o: Yes, about ten percent are vegetarian, and two guests have a serious nut allergy.
There are a few vegans and one person who needs gluten-free food.
Not as far as I know, but I will double-check with the guests and come back to you.
br: For allergies, we prepare those dishes separately and label every item clearly.
We have plenty of plant-based options, so that is easy.
Please let us know at least a week before the event.

budget.m: For that, our menu starts at eighteen euros per person. Does that fit your budget?
o: That is slightly above what we planned. Is there any flexibility on the price?
That sounds acceptable, but could you tell me what the price includes?
It fits our budget, provided that service and drinks are included.
br: We could look at a discount for a larger order.
The price includes food, staff and setting up. Drinks are extra.

discount.m: If you order for fifty or more, I can offer ten percent off. Otherwise, we could simplify the dessert. Which would you prefer?
o: We will not reach fifty guests, so I would rather simplify the dessert to keep the price down.
Ten percent would be perfect, so I will try to invite a few more colleagues.
Could you do the discount for forty-five guests if I confirm the booking today?
br: Sure, we can replace it with a fruit platter. That saves two euros each.
Great, a bigger group is always more fun.
If you confirm today with a deposit, I think I can make an exception.

logistics.m: Now the practical side. Where will the event take place, and what time should we deliver and set up?
o: It will be in our office on the fourth floor, and the lunch should be ready by twelve thirty.
The venue is a rented hall, so you will need to check what equipment they provide in the kitchen.
We would like you to arrive an hour early, and we need access via the goods lift because of the stairs.
br: We will visit or call the venue first, to see what we can use.
Noted. We will need parking access for the van and the name of a contact person.
Perfect. We will arrive at eleven thirty to set up.

wrap.m: I will send you a quote by email today. To book the date, we need a twenty percent deposit. Is there anything else you would like to ask?
o: No, that is everything for now. Could you please send the quote before noon tomorrow?
Yes, what happens if we need to change the number of guests at the last minute?
What is your cancellation policy in case the event has to be postponed?
br: You can change the numbers up to seventy-two hours before without any extra cost.
If you cancel with more than two weeks’ notice, we refund the deposit in full.
Of course. I will make sure it goes out first thing.

calls.end: Thank you for choosing Green Table. We look forward to feeding your team!

calls.title: Postponing an important meeting
calls.role: a business partner whose meeting you need to move
phrases: I am afraid I have to ask for a postponement.
a tactful way to move a meeting
I fully appreciate how inconvenient this is.
Would that work for you, provided that…?
To make up for it, I would be glad to…
Let me summarise what we have agreed.

hi.m: Hello, it is Carlos from Nordlight. I got your message about tomorrow’s meeting. I hope nothing is wrong?
o: Thanks for calling back. Unfortunately, something urgent has come up on our side, and I wonder whether we could move tomorrow’s meeting to later in the week.
Good to hear from you. I am afraid I have to ask for a postponement, as one of our key colleagues has fallen ill and the presentation would not be complete without her.
Thank you for getting back to me so quickly. Our legal team has asked for another review of the contract, so it would be better not to meet until that is finished.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Please pass on my best wishes.
I see. I must say that is a little unexpected at this stage.

concern.m: I must be frank. We have already cleared our schedules, and the delay may affect our own internal timeline. Can you reassure me that this will not put the deal at risk?
o: I completely understand your frustration, and I can assure you that our commitment to the project has not changed in any way.
I appreciate your candour. The delay is purely procedural, and I am confident that we will still be able to sign within the original timeframe.
You are right to raise that. To make up for the inconvenience, I would be glad to share our draft proposal in advance, so your team can start preparing.
br: Thank you, that does reassure me.
Good. As long as the timeline holds, I can be flexible.
That is a constructive gesture. I would welcome that.

when.m: So when would suit you? I am free on Thursday morning or the following Monday, but Friday is out of the question.
o: Thursday morning would be ideal, provided that you can accommodate a slightly shorter session of an hour and a half.
I would prefer the following Monday, as it would give us the time we need to do this properly without rushing.
Let me check with my team, but I suspect Thursday would work. Could I confirm by the end of the day?
br: Of course. I would need an answer by five, if possible.
Monday is fine, although it is a tight week.
Thursday works. I can shift my other call.

flex.m: There is one more thing. If we met remotely instead, we could keep to the original date. Would you be open to a video call, or is it essential to meet face to face?
o: A video call would be perfectly acceptable for the first part, but I would value an in-person session to discuss the contract details.
Honestly, I think face to face would be better for the relationship, so I would rather not rush it, even if it costs us a few days.
A video call would work if we limit the agenda to the main points, and then save the sensitive items for a follow-up meeting.
br: Understood. Relationships matter in these deals. We can wait.
A shorter agenda is sensible. I will draw one up.

confirm.m: Let me recap, so that we are on the same page. Could you summarise what we have agreed and what happens next?
o: To summarise, we will meet on Thursday at ten, I will send the revised agenda by tomorrow noon, and you will receive our draft proposal in advance.
So we have agreed to move the meeting, and I will confirm the final time in writing today. Meanwhile, I will make sure your team has all the documents they need.
In short, the meeting moves to Monday morning, we keep to the original signing date, and I will brief my team so nothing is lost in the handover.
br: Thank you. A written confirmation will be helpful.
Good. Please keep me posted on any change.

wrap.m: Thank you. Before we hang up, is there anything that might help us avoid a similar situation in future?
o: Perhaps we could agree on a shared calendar and a buffer day before every major meeting, so that last-minute changes do not become a problem.
I would suggest that we both nominate a deputy, so that an absence does not delay the entire process.
Thank you for your patience and flexibility. I will make sure this does not happen again, and I look forward to seeing you on Thursday.
br: A shared calendar is a good idea. I will ask my assistant to set it up.
A deputy is sensible. We both lose time when one person is out.
The pleasure is mine. See you then.

calls.end: Thanks for understanding. Speak soon.

calls.title: Signing up as a volunteer
calls.role: a volunteer coordinator at a community project
phrases: I would like to find out how I could contribute.
I could commit to two hours every Saturday.
I would need some flexibility during exam periods.
Could you send me the handbook in advance?

hi.m: Hello, Riverside Community Project, Ama speaking. How can I help?
o: Hello, I came across your call for volunteers online, and I would like to find out how I could contribute, given that I only have evenings and weekends free.
Good afternoon. I have been thinking about giving something back to the community for a while, and I would like to know which roles you still need to fill.
Hi, I am a teacher by profession, so I am especially interested in any education projects you might be running, though I am open to other roles.
br: That is a real asset. We are short of homework club mentors.
Flexibility is good. We have roles at both times.
We have a few, from sorting donations to mentoring.

skills.m: Do you have any experience working with children or with people from different backgrounds? And do you have a recent background check?
o: I have taught for eight years in a secondary school, and I hold a current background check certificate that I can share with you.
Not formally, but I have helped my neighbours’ children with their homework for years, and I am happy to complete any training you require.
I have worked with multicultural teams for a long time, although I have never done a safeguarding course, which I would be keen to take.
br: Excellent. That will speed up the process considerably.
We run a short induction course every month.

roles.m: We have three main areas: the food bank, the homework club, and our weekend repair café. Which of these appeals to you most, and why?
o: The homework club appeals to me most, because my teaching experience would be useful and I enjoy working with young people.
I would lean towards the repair café, since I like practical work and I would love to learn from the experienced volunteers.
To be honest, I would be happy with anything, but the food bank seems to address the most urgent need, so I would like to start there.
br: Our mentors make a real difference. The children look forward to it.
The repair café is lively. People bring in everything from toasters to bicycles.
The food bank is the heart of what we do, and we can always use more hands.

commitment.m: How much time could you realistically commit to? We would rather have a steady two hours a week than a burst of enthusiasm that fades after a month.
o: I could commit to two hours every Saturday morning, and I would be willing to cover extra shifts occasionally if you were short-staffed.
Realistically, I can do one evening a week, but my schedule changes seasonally, so I would need some flexibility during exam periods.
I would like to start with a three-month trial period, to see whether the role suits me and whether I am useful to you.
br: That regularity is exactly what we need. Thank you.
We can work with that. Many of our volunteers have changing schedules.
A trial period is a sensible way to begin, for both sides.

concerns.m: Is there anything you are worried about, or anything that would make it difficult for you to take part?
o: My only concern is that I do not want to take a place from someone with more experience, as I am new to community work.
I do not have a car, so I would need to know whether the venue is accessible by public transport and what time the last bus leaves.
I would like to know what support is available if a situation becomes emotionally difficult, because I want to be useful rather than overwhelmed.
br: The centre is two minutes from the tram stop. Evenings are well served.
We hold a short debrief after each session, and there is a volunteer lead you can always talk to.
Please do not worry. Enthusiasm and reliability matter far more than experience.

wrap.m: That all sounds promising. Shall I put you down for an induction session next Wednesday evening, and what should I write as your preferred first role?
o: Wednesday evening works well for me, and I would like to start with the homework club, if there is still a place.
I am afraid Wednesday clashes with a prior commitment. Would there be an induction on a weekend instead?
That would be wonderful. Could you also email me the schedule and the volunteer handbook so that I can prepare in advance?
br: No problem. We have an induction on Saturday at ten.
Of course. I will send them this afternoon.
Lovely. I will put you down for Wednesday at six.

calls.end: Thank you so much. We are very glad to have you with us.

calls.title: Asking a colleague to cover your shift
calls.role: a friendly colleague at work
phrases: ask someone to work in your place
I would be happy to return the favour.
say you need time before you answer

hi.m: Hi! You wanted to talk to me? You look a bit stressed.
o: Yes, I need a big favour from you.
Hi! Could you possibly cover my shift on Friday?
I have a problem with my schedule this week.
br: Cover your shift? Tell me more.
Of course, what is going on?

why.m: Which shift is it, and what happened?
o: It is the evening shift on Friday, and I have a family event.
My sister is getting married on Friday, so I cannot work that night.
I have a medical appointment that I could not move to another day.
br: Congratulations to her! That sounds important.
Oh, I hope everything is fine.

hours.m: I usually go home at six on Fridays. How long would the shift be?
o: It runs from four until ten, so six hours in total.
About five hours, and you would get the late bonus.
I think it is until closing time, around ten o’clock.
br: The bonus is nice, but my evening matters to me too.
That is quite late for me.

offer.m: I could do it if you cover my Sunday morning shift in return. Would that work?
o: Yes, that works for me. I can take your Sunday shift.
Could we swap instead? I would rather work Sunday than Saturday.
Let me check my calendar first, and I will tell you tonight.
br: Great, then it is a deal.
A swap is fine with me.
Sure, no rush. Just let me know today.

boss.m: We should tell the manager so the schedule is updated. Who will do it?
o: I will send her an email this afternoon with both changes.
Could we go and speak to her together after lunch?
I will tell her and copy you so everything is clear.
br: Good idea. Then we both have it in writing.
Fine. Let us catch her right after lunch.

thanks.m: Okay, that is settled. Anything else you need from me?
o: No, thank you so much. I owe you one.
Just a reminder about the keys, because I will not be there.
Thanks a lot. Next time, I will cover for you.
br: Good point. I will pick them up from the desk.
Do not worry about it. That is what colleagues are for.

calls.end: No problem at all. Enjoy the wedding, or the day off, whatever it is!

calls.title: Ordering and bargaining at a market stall
calls.role: a fruit seller at an outdoor market
phrases: show you are happy with the price

hi.m: Good morning! Fresh mangoes and oranges today. What would you like?
o: I would like some mangoes, please.
Are the oranges sweet today?
How much are the mangoes?
br: Very sweet! Please, try one piece.
The mangoes are four dollars a kilo.
Good choice. They are very fresh.

amount.m: How many kilos do you want?
o: Two kilos, please.
Half a kilo is enough.
One kilo of mangoes, please.
br: Two kilos. That is a lot. Your family must like fruit!

price.m: That makes eight dollars. Is that okay for you?
o: It is a little expensive. Can you make it cheaper?
Eight dollars is fine for me.
Can I get a discount for two kilos?
br: Hmm, okay. For you, seven dollars. Last price.
Wonderful. You are a nice customer.

deal.m: Seven dollars. This is my best price. Do we have a deal?
o: Yes, that is a good deal.
Can you give me one orange for free?
Six dollars, and I will come back tomorrow.
br: Ha, you are clever! Okay, one orange for you.
Six is too low. Six fifty, and I add a small bag.

pay.m: Here is your bag. Do you have small money?
o: I only have a big note. Sorry.
Yes, here is ten dollars.
Do you have change for twenty dollars?
br: No problem. I have change. Here you are.
Thank you. Here are your three dollars back.

calls.end: Thank you! Come back tomorrow. I will have fresh pineapples!

calls.title: Booking a hair appointment
calls.role: a receptionist at a hair salon
phrases: I would like to book an appointment.
Do you have anything on Saturday?
Can I change it to Monday?

hi.m: Good afternoon, Bella Hair Studio. How can I help you?
o: I would like to book an appointment, please.
Hello. Do you have a free time this week?
Can I make an appointment for a haircut?
br: Let me look at the calendar.
Of course. I can help you with that.

service.m: What would you like to have done?
o: Just a trim, please.
I want a haircut and a wash.
I would like to change my hair colour.
br: A colour takes longer, about two hours.
A cut and wash takes about forty minutes.

day.m: We have Thursday at ten, or Saturday at two. Which one is better?
o: Saturday at two is better for me.
Thursday morning is good, thank you.
Do you have anything on Friday?
br: Let me see. Friday at four is free.

stylist.m: Do you prefer a certain stylist, or is anyone fine?
o: Anyone is fine for me.
I would like Linda, if she is free.
Is there a stylist who speaks English?
br: Linda is very popular, but she is free then.
Yes, all our stylists speak English.
Okay, I will choose someone good.

name.m: Great. Can I have your name and a phone number, please?
o: My name is Anna Nguyen.
It is Tom, and my number is zero nine one.
Can I send a message instead of a call?
br: Yes, we can send a text to remind you.
Thank you, I have it now.

calls.end: You are all booked. See you soon!

calls.title: Reporting a lost wallet to the police
calls.role: a police officer at the station
phrases: I would like to report a lost wallet.
It is made of black leather.
I need a copy of the report.

hi.m: Good evening. What can I do for you?
o: I would like to report a lost wallet.
I think my wallet was stolen on the bus.
Hello. I lost my wallet somewhere in the city centre.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Pickpockets are a problem on that line.
I understand. Let us see what we can do.

where.m: When and where did you last see it?
o: I last saw it at lunchtime, when I paid in a café.
I am sure I had it on the bus at around six o’clock.
I noticed it was missing when I got off the train.
br: We will call the café and ask. Which one was it?
Public transport has a lost property office. We will contact them too.

describe.m: Can you describe the wallet, and what was inside?
o: It is a black leather wallet with a silver button.
Inside there were two bank cards, my ID and about fifty dollars.
It is small and brown, and it has my student card inside.
br: Documents are the biggest worry. We note them in the report.
That helps. I have written the description down.

cards.m: Have you contacted your bank about the cards yet?
o: Not yet. Should I cancel my cards now?
Yes, I called the bank and blocked both cards.
No, I came straight here. What should I do first?
br: Yes, please call them right away. Then you are protected.
Very good. That was the right thing to do.

copy.m: I have finished the report. Is there anything else you need?
o: Could I have a copy of the report for my insurance?
Yes. What happens if someone finds the wallet?
Please, can you give me a reference number?
br: Of course. Here is a printed copy with the reference number.
We will call you on this number. Please keep your phone on.
The reference number is on the top of this page.

calls.end: I hope we find it soon. Take care.

calls.title: Asking a landlord to fix the heating
calls.role: a busy landlord who owns several flats
phrases: The heating has not been working since…
say how long the problem exists
I am afraid it cannot wait.
show that the problem is urgent
It says in the agreement that…
When can I expect someone to come?
I would appreciate a written confirmation.

hi.m: Hello, this is Ms Bell. I got your message. Something about the heating?
o: Yes, the heating has not been working since last Monday.
Thank you for calling back. The radiators are completely cold.
Hello. I am calling because the heating in my flat has broken down.
br: Since last Monday? That is quite a while. I did not know that.
Oh dear, in this weather that must be unpleasant.
I see. Let us find out what is wrong.

tried.m: Have you tried bleeding the radiators or checking the boiler pressure?
o: Yes, I bled all the radiators, but nothing has changed.
The boiler shows an error code, and the pressure is almost zero.
I followed the instructions on the boiler, but it still will not start.
br: That sounds like a fault in the boiler itself. It needs an engineer.
Then it is not a simple fix. I will need a professional.

urgent.m: I can send someone next week. Would that be acceptable?
o: I am afraid it cannot wait that long, because it is below ten degrees at night.
Next week is too late for us. We have a baby in the flat.
Could someone come earlier? Otherwise I will need to buy electric heaters.
br: A baby? Then I understand it is urgent. Let me see who is free.
Please do not buy anything yet. I will arrange it quickly.
Understood. I will call the engineer and see what is possible.

date.m: The engineer can come on Thursday between nine and twelve. Can you be there?
o: Thursday morning is fine, and I will be at home all day.
I work on Thursday, but my neighbour can let him in.
Could we move it to the afternoon, if that is possible?
br: Good. Please send me her number so he can call her.
Let me check. Yes, two to five is possible.

rent.m: Is there anything else about the flat I should know?
o: Yes, the agreement says the repair is your responsibility, so please cover the cost.
Because we had no heating for days, could we talk about reducing this month’s rent?
No, that is all, but I would appreciate a written confirmation of the visit.
br: I cannot promise that, but I will think about a small reduction.
You are right. The repair is on me, of course.
Certainly. I will email you the time and the engineer’s name today.

calls.end: I am sorry for the trouble. I will make sure it is fixed this week.

calls.title: Introducing yourself at a conference
calls.role: a fellow delegate you meet at a coffee break
phrases: That is right up my street.
I would love to pick your brain about…

hi.m: Hello, I do not think we have met. Carlos Mendez, from the Madrid office. And you are?
o: Nice to meet you, Carlos. I am an analyst, and I specialise in energy markets.
Pleased to meet you. I lead the data team at a logistics company in Vietnam.
Hello, Carlos. I am a freelance consultant, mostly working with small manufacturers.
br: Energy markets, fascinating. Prices have been so unpredictable lately.
Logistics and data, now that is a powerful combination.
A consultant, so you probably see a lot of different companies.

why.m: And what brought you to this conference in particular?
o: Mainly the panel on supply chain resilience, since it is directly relevant to my current project.
To be honest, I came to broaden my network and hear what other regions are doing.
A colleague recommended the keynote speaker, and I was curious to see her in person.
br: That session was packed yesterday. I have heard it was excellent.
Networking is half the value of these events, in my experience.
Her talk was brilliant. The part about automation really stayed with me.

session.m: Which session has been the most useful for you so far?
o: The workshop on forecasting gave me several practical insights I can use at work immediately.
Honestly, the best conversations have happened in the corridors rather than in the sessions.
The opening keynote was inspiring, though I wish there had been more time for questions.
br: I missed that one. Would you mind telling me the main points?
That is so true. The unplanned chats often lead to real projects.
I agree. Q and A is always cut short, which is a shame.

collab.m: We are looking for partners in Southeast Asia. Do you see any room for collaboration?
o: Definitely. We have strong local contacts, so we could collaborate on a pilot study next year.
It is possible, although I would need to discuss the details with my director first.
I would love to pick your brain about the regulations before we go any further.
br: That sounds promising. A pilot is a low-risk way to begin.
Of course. Take your time, there is no pressure from our side.
Happy to help. The rules differ a lot between countries, so it is worth planning.

followup.m: I have to go to the next session, but I would like to continue this conversation.
o: Let us exchange details, and I will follow up with an email by the end of the week.
Here is my card. Perhaps we could arrange a video call once we are both back at the office.
Certainly. Are you free for dinner tonight? We could discuss it properly then.
br: Dinner would be lovely. Shall we say eight, at the hotel restaurant?
Excellent. I will look out for it and reply quickly.
Perfect. I will keep an eye out for your message.

calls.end: It was a real pleasure talking with you. Enjoy the rest of the conference!

calls.title: Giving feedback to a team member
calls.role: a talented but sometimes careless team member
phrases: I would like to share some feedback.
What you do really well is…
One area where I see room to grow…
Let us agree on a next step.

hi.m: Hi, you wanted a word? I hope I have not done anything wrong.
o: Not at all. I would simply like to share some feedback on the last quarter.
No need to worry. This is a regular check-in, and I want to start with the positives.
Thanks for coming. I would like us to look at how the project is going together.
br: Okay, that is a relief. I am glad to hear it.
Sure, feedback is always welcome, and I want to improve.
Of course. I have some thoughts on it as well.

strength.m: Great. So what have I been doing well?
o: Your presentations are excellent, and clients clearly trust you because you explain things so clearly.
You have shown real initiative this quarter, especially when you took over the onboarding project.
What you do really well is stay calm under pressure, which the whole team has noticed.
br: Thank you. I put a lot of effort into the presentations.
I enjoyed that project, actually. It taught me a lot.
That is kind of you to say. It does not always feel calm inside!

concern.m: That is good to hear. Is there anything you would like me to do differently?
o: One area where I see room to grow is attention to detail, because a few reports contained avoidable errors.
Two deadlines slipped recently, and I would like us to understand why that happened.
I have noticed you sometimes stay quiet in meetings, and your ideas deserve to be heard.
br: You are right. I have been rushing the final checks, and I regret that.
I underestimated the workload, and I should have told you earlier.
I tend to hold back when senior people are present. I would like to change that.

view.m: I take your point. Honestly, I have felt a bit overloaded lately.
o: Thank you for being open about it. Let us look at your workload and see what we can take off your plate.
I appreciate your honesty. How do you see the balance between the projects you currently have?
That is important to know. Next time, please tell me as soon as you feel the pressure building.
br: That would really help. I have three big tasks running in parallel.
Two of them could wait. The client report is the real priority.
I will, I promise. I did not want to look like I could not cope.

plan.m: So what do you suggest we do from here?
o: Let us agree on two next steps: a short weekly check-in and a second pair of eyes on your reports.
I suggest we review the workload on Friday and decide which task moves to someone else.
Why don’t you propose a plan yourself, and then we will refine it together next week?
br: That sounds fair. A regular check-in will keep me accountable.
Good idea. I will list everything I am working on before Friday.
I like that. It gives me ownership, and I will have it ready by Monday.

calls.end: Thank you for talking so openly. I feel much more motivated now.

calls.title: Declining an invitation politely
calls.role: a friendly neighbour who invites you to a party
phrases: Thank you so much for inviting me.
Unfortunately, I will not be able to make it.
Can I take a rain check?
ask to do it another time
I hope you have a great time.

hi.m: Hey! We are having a barbecue on Saturday afternoon. Would you like to come?
o: Thank you so much for inviting me.
That sounds lovely. What time does it start?
Oh, that is very kind of you. Who else is coming?
br: It starts at three, but you can come any time.
Mostly neighbours and a few friends from work.
You are welcome! It will be relaxed and fun.

refuse.m: So can we count on you? We need to know how many people are coming.
o: Unfortunately, I will not be able to make it this Saturday.
I am sorry, but I already have plans for that afternoon.
I would love to, but I have to visit my parents this weekend.
br: Oh, what a pity. We will miss you.
Ah, no problem. I understand you are busy.
Family comes first. That is completely fine.

why.m: Is it something we could work around, like coming later in the evening?
o: That is kind, but I will be exhausted after a long drive.
I am afraid the evening does not work either, as I have an early start on Sunday.
Thank you for offering, but I really need a quiet weekend to rest.
br: That makes sense. Driving all day is tiring.
Of course. Everyone needs to recharge sometimes.

raincheck.m: No worries. Maybe another time then?
o: Yes, can I take a rain check for the next one?
I would love that. Let me invite you for coffee next week.
Definitely, and please keep me on the list for the next party.
br: Absolutely. You are on the list for the next barbecue.
Coffee sounds great. Let us arrange it on Monday.
Of course, you are always welcome.

close.m: Alright. Anything I can bring you tomorrow, since you are not coming?
o: No, thank you. I hope you all have a great time.
Just send me a photo of the food, and I will be jealous!
Please say hello to everyone from me.
br: Ha, I will send you the best one.
I will! They will be happy to hear from you.
Thank you. That is very thoughtful.

calls.end: Take care, and see you around the building!

calls.title: Explaining a delay to a client
calls.role: a client who expects your delivery on Friday
phrases: I would like to apologise for the delay.
say sorry at a formal level
We would like to make it up to you.

hi.m: Hello, this is Ama from Brightline. I was expecting our order on Friday. Is it on its way?
o: Hello, Ama. I would like to apologise, but the delivery will be delayed.
Thank you for calling. I am afraid there is a problem with your order.
Good morning. I was just about to call you with an update on the delivery.
br: A delay? That is a serious concern for us.
A problem? Please tell me exactly what happened.
Good, then please give me the details right now.

cause.m: Why exactly is it late? We have a launch event on Monday.
o: The delay is due to our supplier, who sent the wrong components last week.
A storm closed the port, so the shipment is stuck for at least three days.
We found a quality problem in the final check, and we refused to send faulty goods.
br: So the mistake was on your side, not mine. That is frustrating.
Weather is nobody’s fault, but I still need a solution.
I appreciate that you did not send faulty goods, but timing is everything.

date.m: The event cannot move. What date can you honestly promise?
o: We have revised the timeline, and I can promise delivery by Tuesday at noon.
If we use express transport, I can guarantee that you receive it on Monday morning.
I cannot give an exact date yet, but I will confirm one by this evening.
br: Tuesday is after my launch. That does not help me at all.
Monday morning is tight, but it could work. Is that firm?
I need more certainty than that. Evening is the latest I can wait.

cost.m: And who pays for the extra shipping and for the inconvenience?
o: We will cover the express shipping, and I would like to offer you a ten percent discount.
Our company takes full responsibility, so we will compensate you for the extra costs.
I would need to check with my manager, but I am confident we can find a fair solution.
br: That is a fair start. Please put it in writing.
I appreciate that. Taking responsibility matters to us.
Please do, and call me back within the hour.

update.m: Fine. How will I know the truth about the delivery from now on?
o: I will keep you updated by phone every morning until the goods arrive.
You will receive a tracking link today, and I am personally available all week.
I will send a written confirmation with the new date within the hour.
br: Every morning is perfect. Call before nine, please.
A tracking link will help my team a lot.
Good. Then I have it in writing.

calls.end: Thank you for being straight with me. Please do not let it happen again.

calls.title: Making a travel insurance claim
calls.role: a claims adviser at a travel insurance company
phrases: I would like to make a claim.
It should be covered under my policy.
How long does the process take?
Could you confirm that in writing?

hi.m: Thank you for calling Safe Journey Insurance. How can I help you today?
o: I would like to make a claim under my travel policy.
Hello. My luggage was damaged on my flight, and I need to know how to claim.
Good morning. I had to cancel my trip because I fell ill.
br: I am sorry about your luggage. Let us go through the details.
I am sorry to hear that. I hope you are feeling better now.
Of course. I will need a few details first.

incident.m: Please describe what happened, with dates and places.
o: On the fifth of May, my suitcase came off the carousel in Lisbon with a broken wheel and a torn side.
I became ill on the second day of the holiday, and the doctor ordered me to rest for a week.
I reported the damage to the airline desk immediately, and they gave me a written report.
br: Thank you. Damage like that is usually covered, if it was reported quickly.
A medical certificate will be important for this claim.
Excellent. Prompt reporting is exactly what the policy requires.

cover.m: Could you tell me which policy type you have, and what you paid for the item?
o: I have the premium cover, and the suitcase cost about two hundred euros.
I paid for the standard policy, and it should be covered under the baggage section.
I do not have the receipt with me, but I can find the bank statement.
br: Good, both levels include baggage, with an excess of fifty euros.
A bank statement is acceptable proof of purchase.
Understood. The refund will be based on the item’s current value.

docs.m: We will need documentation. Which of these can you provide?
o: I have attached the photos, the airline report and my boarding pass in an email.
I can send you the repair quote, along with the original receipt, by tomorrow.
Unfortunately, I threw the suitcase away, but I have photos from before and after.
br: That is a complete set. It should make the process faster.
Perfect. Send them to the address I give you.
Photos are sufficient in this case, though you should keep items in future.

time.m: Is there anything else you would like to ask?
o: How long does the process usually take before the money reaches my account?
Could you confirm everything we discussed in writing, please?
What happens if my claim is rejected? Can I appeal?
br: Normally ten working days after we receive all the documents.
Certainly. You will receive a confirmation email within the hour.
You can appeal within thirty days, with any extra evidence.

calls.end: Thank you for your patience. I will make sure your claim is processed promptly.

calls.title: Asking a professor for an extension
calls.role: a university professor in office hours
phrases: I wanted to ask about an extension.
Would it be possible to submit it on…?
I understand if it is not possible.

hi.m: Come in, please. What can I do for you?
o: I wanted to ask about an extension for my essay.
Good afternoon. Could we talk about the assignment deadline?
I am having some difficulty finishing my paper on time.
br: An extension? Let us hear what the situation is.
I see. Tell me where you are with it.

reason.m: Can you tell me the reason? I need to be fair to all the students.
o: I was ill for a week, and I missed several library days.
I have had three exams and a family emergency in the past two weeks.
My laptop broke last Friday, and I lost part of my work.
br: I am sorry to hear that. Have you seen a doctor?
That is a lot to handle. I hope your family is okay.
That is unfortunate. Did you not have a backup?

progress.m: How much of the essay have you already completed?
o: I have finished the research and written about half of the draft.
I have a full outline, and the introduction is already done.
Honestly, I have only started, but I know what I want to write.
br: That is good progress. You are not starting from nothing.
A clear outline is already a strong foundation.
Thank you for being honest. That is better than pretending.

newdate.m: The deadline is this Friday. What would you consider a reasonable new date?
o: Would it be possible to submit it next Wednesday instead?
I could hand it in on Monday morning, if that works for you.
Five extra days would be enough for me to finish and proofread.
br: Wednesday is a bit long. Let me think about what is fair.
Monday morning is acceptable, I think.
Five days is generous, but I understand why you need it.

decision.m: Alright. I will give you until Monday at noon. No further extension after that.
o: Thank you so much for your understanding.
I really appreciate it. I will not let you down.
Monday at noon is perfect. I will email you the essay as soon as I finish.
br: Good. Please also send a short note when you submit it.
I trust you. Good luck with the writing.
You are welcome. Now go and write!

calls.end: Good luck. I look forward to reading your work.

calls.title: Handling a billing mistake with a phone company
calls.role: a customer service agent at a mobile phone company
phrases: I was charged for something I did not use.
Could you look into this for me?
I would like a full refund.
I would like to speak to a supervisor.
Please send me a confirmation by email.

hi.m: Thank you for calling TelSpark customer care. How may I help you?
o: I am calling about my latest bill, because there is a charge I do not understand.
Hello. I think there is a mistake on my statement this month.
I was charged for roaming, although I did not leave the country.
br: Roaming charges can sometimes appear by mistake. Let me check your account.
I am sorry about that. I will pull up your statement now.
I will gladly explain it. Could you give me your account number?

detail.m: I can see a charge of eighty dollars on the fourteenth. What exactly is the problem?
o: My plan includes unlimited data, so I should not have paid any extra fee.
I have never used that service, and I certainly did not agree to the charge.
The amount is more than three times my normal monthly bill, which seems wrong.
br: You are right, your plan covers data. Let me look at what it says.
Understood. It might be a service you were switched onto by accident.
That is a big difference. I can see why you called.

cause.m: It seems a premium subscription was added to your line. Did you sign up for it?
o: No, I did not sign up for anything. Could you look into how it was added?
I might have clicked an advert by accident, but I never confirmed a payment.
Absolutely not. I always read the terms before I agree to a service.
br: Certainly. It was activated through a text message link.
That happens often. Those links are not always clear.
Then I believe you. We will treat it as an error.

fix.m: I can remove the subscription. What would you like us to do about the charge?
o: I would like a full refund of the eighty dollars, paid back to my card.
A credit on next month’s bill would be acceptable, if it is applied automatically.
I would also like compensation, because I have lost a lot of time on this.
br: A refund is possible. It usually reaches the card in five days.
I can apply that credit today, and it will show on the next bill.
I cannot offer that myself, but I can add a goodwill credit.

escalate.m: I can refund fifty dollars now. The rest needs a manager’s approval.
o: I would like to speak to a supervisor, because the entire amount was your error.
Fine, but please send me a confirmation by email so everything is on record.
Could you open a formal dispute so that the full amount is reviewed?
br: I will transfer you. Please stay on the line, it should take two minutes.
Of course. You will receive the email within the hour.
I will open it now. You will get a reference number by email.

calls.end: I am sorry for the mistake, and thank you for your patience today.
